## New Year, New Game: 5 Skillz Goals to Set for 2027


- by Skillz
- Nov. 20, 2026
- 4 min read


-
-
-
-


A new year is a natural time to reset, and that goes for how you play, too. Most resolutions fade by February because they are too big or too vague. Gameplay goals are different. They are small, you can measure them, and you see progress quickly.


Whether you are new to Skillz or you have been competing for years, these five goals will help you play smarter in 2027. Pick one or two to start. You can always add more once they become habits.


## **Goal 1: Try a Game Type You Have Never Played**


It is easy to stick with the one game you know. Branching out makes you a more well-rounded player, because each game type builds a different skill. Card games like Blackjack by Skillz reward planning and smart decisions. Bingo games like Blackout Bingo reward fast pattern spotting. Puzzle and arcade games like Bubble Universe reward clean, efficient moves.


Make it a goal to try at least one new game type in January. Play it in practice mode first, learn the rules, and see whether it fits your style. You might find a new favorite, and the skills you pick up often apply to the games you already love.


## **Goal 2: Build a Simple Practice Routine**


Consistent players are rarely the ones who play the most. They are the ones who practice with a plan. Your routine does not need to be complicated. A good starting point:


- **Warm up first.** Play a couple of practice games before you jump into competitive matches.


- **Focus on one skill per session.** In Dominoes Gold, that might be tracking which tiles have been played. In Blackout Bingo, it might be speed.


- **Keep sessions short and regular.** A few focused sessions a week will improve your game more than one long marathon.


Write your routine down or set a reminder on your phone. The goal is to make practice automatic.


## **Goal 3: Learn Something From Every Loss**


Every player loses. What separates improving players from everyone else is what they do next. This year, make it a goal to treat each loss as feedback instead of frustration.


After a tough match, watch the replay and look for the moment the game turned. Did you rush a decision? Miss a pattern? Hold a card or tile too long? Pick one thing to do differently next time. Over a few weeks, those small adjustments add up.


## **Goal 4: Test Yourself in a New Format**


If you always play head-to-head matches, try a Bracket tournament. If you always play Bracket tournaments, try a head-to-head match against a single opponent. Each format tests you differently.


- **Head-to-head matches** pair you with one opponent at a similar skill level, so every decision counts.


- **Bracket tournaments put you** against a larger field and reward consistency over several rounds.


Because Skillz matches players based on skill, you will face opponents at your level as you try something new, not seasoned pros on day one.


## **Goal 5: Keep the Game Fun**


The best goal of all is to enjoy the time you spend playing. Skill-based games reward focus, so play when you are fresh and can give the game your full attention. Decide ahead of time how long you want to play, and stick to it. Taking breaks keeps your head clear and your play sharp.


A goal that keeps the game fun is the one that will last all year.


## **How to Track Your Progress**


A goal is easier to keep when you can see it working. Check in with yourself at the end of each month and ask:


1. Did I try something new this month?


2. Do I understand why I win or lose more often than I used to?


3. Am I still enjoying the time I spend playing?


If the answers are yes, you are on track. If not, adjust the goal and keep going. Progress counts more than perfection.


## **Start Your Year Strong**


A new year brings new opponents, new challenges, and new chances to grow as a player. Choose your goals, start with practice, and see how far your skills can take you in 2027.


Ready to get started? Download a new Skillz game today and make it your first goal of the year.
